propositions: Non-bug tickets (task/story/epic) lack a truthful administrative close path; operators resort to --force for ~25 FORCE_CLOSE audit records annually with ADMINISTRATIVE intent (duplicate, obsolete, superseded, wontfix).
Completion verification cannot PASS administrative-disposition closes; the failure message never surfaces the narrow existing path (class-gated by type and limited vocabulary) nor suggests it exists.

The --class mechanism must extend to cover obsolete (premise expired), superseded (replaced by live ticket), and wontfix (deliberate decision) with per-class reason requirements; vocabulary must be single-sourced across schemas, enums, and enforcement points.

Reason-only administrative closes (obsolete/wontfix) must skip completion verifier checks and mint signed attestations from (class + reason); replacement-bearing classes (duplicate/superseded) must demand live replacement links.

Write-side enforcement must gate non-bug closes to ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES vocabulary only; obsolete/wontfix must require a reason persisted as close_reason (distinct from force_close_reason) on the close event.
Close-gate refusal messages must enumerate the applicable --class values truthfully for the ticket type so operators discover the administrative path without --force.
